ASSESSMENT METHODOLOGY
CONFIDENTIAL · FOR HIRING REVIEW
Partner Growth Manager · Apty Prepared 6 August 2026
This page sets out how the candidate was assessed. The page that follows covers her in full. Every point is drawn from a recorded, structured screening call
rather than from a resume. 
What the role demands
The brief is a hands-on individual contributor rather than a people manager: partner prospecting owned end to end across North America with the United
States primary, accounts identified and tiered, decision-makers engaged directly, roughly three qualified partner meetings created every week, and clean
context handed to the internal team. Ten dimensions carry that emphasis, weighted to fifty: 
DIMENSION WHAT IT COVERS POINTS
A United States and North America Personal US prospecting ownership, segments, personas, results 7.50
B B2B outbound execution Conversations personally generated, channels, follow-through 6.25
C Account research and prioritisation ICP definition, evidence used, tiering and rejection logic 5.00
D Partner ecosystem and fit Why a firm would refer, resell or implement, and mutual value 6.25
E Outreach and personalisation Message quality, persona fit, sequence and follow-up logic 5.00
F Qualification and partner SQO Reply, meeting and qualified opportunity held apart; handover 7.50
G Target and pipeline orientation Personal target, period, achievement, conversion 3.75
H Funnel analysis and improvement Diagnosis, focused change, evidence that it moved 3.75
I AI, enrichment and workflow Tools put to a decision rather than named 2.50
J CRM and handover discipline Notes, stage management, context passed to sales 2.50
K Authenticity and ownership Specificity, consistency, personal work separated from the team's Gate
Total Capability score 50.00
Authenticity is scored but carries no points; it sets a floor on the recommendation. AI and enrichment are weighted as a method rather than an outcome. The weighting is our
reading of the brief; tell us if your priorities sit differently and we will recalibrate. 
How we assess
Resumes are read against the partner-prospecting screening engine, which weighs described work over tool lists. Those who clear it sit a structured phone
screen: five open questions on a North America outbound motion they owned, a target list built from scratch, a campaign that produced qualified meetings, a
meeting they counted as an opportunity and a partner account pursued, each probed for what they personally researched, wrote, sent and confirmed. Two
practical checks follow: choosing the first twenty firms to approach out of a hundred, and the next step when a US practice head asks for more information. A
tool named without the decision behind it is not evidence of prospecting depth. 
Score and recommendation
Select, 35 to 50 — take to the hiring-manager round.  Grey, 27 to 34 — worth the same round, with the named areas tested inside it.  Reject, below 27 —
unlikely to meet the role's requirements. Grey is not a soft no. Where a profile lands there, the areas still to establish are named rather than general, and for this
candidate there are three, set out overleaf.

Hiring-manager round with focused validation
She runs the outbound motion at her company as the only person in the function, and she reasons about which partners are worth pursuing
from where the partnership earns rather than from list filters. Her clearest campaign evidence sits in the UK and Australia, and the numbers
behind the work are the main thing for the round to settle. 
5 years in B2B sales and business development · currently Channel Sales Manager, APPSeCONNECT, an integration platform connecting e-commerce, CRM, ERP
and accounting systems, where she owns partner prospecting end to end · North America roughly half the mix, UK and Europe 30 per cent, Australia and Canada the
balance · Hyderabad · 30-day notice · 7021938171 · wandharesakshi86@gmail.com

Against the brief — account selection, outreach construction and campaign judgment are evidenced, and the reasoning is her own rather than borrowed. Personal
targets, the line she draws around a qualified opportunity, and how her fit test travels to Apty's ecosystem are what the round should establish. 
What she brings For the next round
From the interview
She checks what a question is reaching for before
answering, and says plainly when she is reasoning from
her current company rather than in general. 
She separates her own work from her team's without
being asked to, naming what the two interns run and what
she does herself. 
Based on a recorded, structured screening call. Prepared for Apty
She owns the outbound motion end to end as the only person in the function: ICP definition, list
building, sequencing and the partner conversation. Sales Navigator carries account-based
outreach, Instantly the cold email, HeyReach the LinkedIn sequences, Apollo and ZoomInfo the list.
Her ICP is the service provider rather than the end user, and she explains why: a Shopify or SAP
Business One implementation partner brings a book of clients who each need integration, so one
partner is worth many direct accounts. Given a hundred US firms she screens first for at least one
connector in common with the stack, then reads LinkedIn presence, headcount growth and
revenue direction, and tiers on project volume, because that is where the partnership pays for both
sides. She works a hot list of sixty to reach twenty for individual research, and would rather run ten
accounts properly than twenty thinly. 
On a US account she went in targeting SAP Business One partners specifically, and found on the
call that the firm carried several other stacks, with more than twenty connectors in common by her
count. Her technical team is now running demos across those stacks. She frames it as choosing
one strategic partner over several transactional ones, and accepts the longer cycle that comes
with a larger firm. 
On a Shopify partner campaign she led with the deployment time that ready-built connectors
save, referenced a recent post from the account, and asked for nothing. The follow-up offers case
studies, demo videos or a live customer reference instead of a calendar link. Three email variants
ran alongside it: recent comparable work, resources and reference, and closed-deal proof. Asked
what she would do if a US practice head replied asking for more information, she answers the
same way: offer a choice of demo, case study or reference rather than send a deck. 
Ahead of December in the UK, where she judged new-account outreach would not land, she
changed the population rather than the volume and ran a re-engagement campaign against lost
and inactive partner accounts. She reports open rates above fifty per cent and meetings from it. 
Targets and conversion. Her results arrive as
descriptions rather than numbers. A target she carried,
and what she delivered against it, would read her pace
against Apty's three-a-week measure. 
What she counts as qualified. She qualifies ahead of
the meeting on stack fit and client need, then closes
the rest in a fifteen-minute discovery. The line
between a reply, a meeting and a qualified opportunity
is worth establishing. 
How the fit test travels. Her first screen is whether a
firm implements something her platform already
connects to, which works where the product is a
connector catalogue. Apty's fit turns on customer
access, implementation capability and service mix.
Worth hearing how she would build the equivalent
here.
